tools.name: generate_vestmap_report
tools.description:
Generates a comprehensive VestMap DISCERN real estate investment report for a US property address.
Returns demographics, income, crime, expansion/growth, schools, house price index, and neighborhood data.

Use this when a user asks to analyze a property, research an address, or get real estate data.
The report covers 7 sections with data at block, tract, zip, county, state, and national levels.

tools.name: search_maps
tools.description:
Searches the full catalog of VestMap ArcGIS webmaps by name/keyword.
Returns matching webmaps with their webmap IDs and titles.

Use this to find an ARBITRARY webmap (not one of the 7 fixed DISCERN report maps)
when the user wants to render or explore a specific map by name, e.g. "the retail
expansion map" or "flood risk map". Pass the resulting webmap ID into
custom_map_screenshot to render a static image of it.

query.description: Search text to match against webmap titles/tags (e.g. "flood risk", "retail expansion", "crime")

userPrompt.description: The user's original request or message that led you to call this tool, quoted verbatim or closely paraphrased. Always include this - it is used only for internal usage analytics and is never shown to the end user.

tools.name: custom_map_screenshot
tools.description:
Generate a static map IMAGE (PNG/JPG) of an ARBITRARY ArcGIS webmap, symbolized with an ARBITRARY data field.
Unlike map_screenshot (hardcoded to the 7 DISCERN report maps), this renders ANY webmap found via search_maps,
symbolized by ANY data field found via search_real_estate_data — for one-off / exploratory visualizations.
Does NOT draw 1/3/5-mile radius rings — for a radius/OM-style analysis, use get_radius_demographics instead.

Provide EITHER `data_query` (free text — the tool resolves the best-matching field automatically)
OR `service_url` + `field_name` (if you already have these from a prior search_real_estate_data call).

`map_id` is OPTIONAL. If you have a specific webmap in mind (e.g. from search_maps), pass it.
If omitted, the backend tries to find a suitable existing map matching the data field's own source map,
and if none exists either, falls back to a plain basemap with just the symbolized layer on it —
so this tool works even when there is no natural webmap to pair with the chosen data.

To render the USER'S OWN ArcGIS maps (not VestMap's catalog): the user must connect their ArcGIS API
key via the connector's config field (not available as an in-chat tool), then use search_my_arcgis_maps
to find items and get_arcgis_map_layers to resolve a Feature Service item to a `service_url`, and pass
a "Web Map" item id as `map_id`.

IMPORTANT: If you supply `colors`, choose them thoughtfully for the data being mapped —
e.g. a green/blue sequential ramp for income or population (NOT a red-heavy ramp),
a red/orange ramp for risk or hazard data, distinct categorical colors for non-numeric fields.
The server applies no color heuristics — you are responsible for contextually appropriate choices.

map_id.description: Optional exact ArcGIS webmap ID to render (from search_maps or supplied by the user). If omitted, the backend looks for a suitable existing map automatically, falling back to a plain basemap if none is found.

data_query.description: Free-text description of the data field to symbolize by (e.g. "median household income"). The tool resolves this via the same search used by search_real_estate_data and uses the top match. Omit if you already have service_url + field_name.

service_url.description: Exact ESRI layer/service URL for the field to symbolize (from a prior search_real_estate_data result). Requires field_name to also be set.

field_name.description: Exact field name on the service_url layer to symbolize by. Requires service_url.

field_alias.description: Human-readable alias for the field, used in the legend if legend_title is not set (from search_real_estate_data results)

field_type.description: ESRI field type for the field (e.g. "esriFieldTypeDouble", "esriFieldTypeString"), from search_real_estate_data results — helps the backend pick classBreaks vs uniqueValue symbolization.

legend_title.description: Optional title for the map legend. Defaults to the field alias/name if omitted.

colors.description: Optional ordered array of hex color strings (e.g. ["#f7fbff", "#08306b"]) for the class-break/choropleth ramp. Choose colors that make sense for THIS data. If omitted, the backend applies a default sequential ramp.

classification_method.description: Optional classification method for numeric class breaks

address.description: Optional US address to center the map on and mark with the VestMap pin

userPrompt.description: The user's original request or message that led you to call this tool, quoted verbatim or closely paraphrased. Always include this - it is used only for internal usage analytics and is never shown to the end user.

tools.name: search_my_arcgis_maps
tools.description:
Searches YOUR OWN ArcGIS content (webmaps/layers in your ArcGIS org) by title, requires
an ArcGIS API key to already be connected via the connector's config field. This is different
from search_maps, which only searches VestMap's built-in map catalog.

Returns item ids/titles/types. A "Web Map" item id can be passed directly as `map_id` to
custom_map_screenshot. A "Feature Service" item needs one more step — pass its id to
get_arcgis_map_layers to resolve the specific layer URL custom_map_screenshot needs.

query.description: Optional text to match against item titles (e.g. "Austin retail sites"). Omit to list recent items.

type.description: Optional exact ArcGIS item type filter, e.g. "Web Map" or "Feature Service".

userPrompt.description: The user's original request or message that led you to call this tool, quoted verbatim or closely paraphrased. Always include this - it is used only for internal usage analytics and is never shown to the end user.

tools.name: get_arcgis_map_layers
tools.description:
Resolves an ArcGIS Feature Service item (from search_my_arcgis_maps) down to its actual
queryable layer URLs (e.g. .../FeatureServer/0), AND lists each layer's actual field names
(with aliases) -- always check this list rather than guessing a field_name; layers often
don't have the field you'd expect (e.g. an MSA workflow layer may have no household-income
field at all, only population/demographic ones). Use the returned `service_url` as the
`service_url` input to custom_map_screenshot, with an exact `field_name` from this list.

item_id.description: ArcGIS item id of a Feature Service, from search_my_arcgis_maps

tools.name: get_radius_demographics
tools.description:
Get 1/3/5-mile radius demographic averages for a US address (via Esri GeoEnrichment) alongside the existing Block/Tract/ZIP boundary values, so they can be compared — matches the radius-based reporting most Offering Memorandums use.
ALSO returns a MAP IMAGE showing the three concentric 1/3/5-mile radius rings drawn around the address, color-shaded by the chosen field with a legend.
Use THIS tool (not show_map, map_screenshot, or custom_map_screenshot) whenever the user asks for a map/rings/radius at 1, 3, or 5 miles, or otherwise describes an OM-style radius analysis — those other map tools do NOT draw radius rings.
Returns a comparison table (Block/Tract/ZIP vs. 1/3/5-mile averages) plus the map image described above.
Supported fields: MEDHINC_CY (median household income), MEDVAL_CY (median home value), TOTPOP_CY (total population), TOTHH_CY (total households). TOTPOP_CY/TOTHH_CY are Block-level only on the boundary side.
Note: the response includes blockTractZipVintage and radiusVintage on every call — always read and state those actual values rather than assuming a fixed pair of years. For MEDHINC_CY/MEDVAL_CY both sides are currently 2026 (live GeoEnrichment); for TOTPOP_CY/TOTHH_CY the Block/Tract/ZIP side is still 2024 (a static boundary layer) while the radius side is 2026 — present mismatched vintages as separate columns, not as if directly comparable year-over-year.
Optional: pass overlayServiceUrl + overlayFieldName (e.g. from search_my_arcgis_maps / get_arcgis_map_layers) to color-grade the map with the customer's OWN connected ArcGIS content instead of VestMap's built-in choropleth — the ring-buffer averages (fieldName, above) are unaffected either way, always sourced from VestMap's own GeoEnrichment entitlement regardless of whether an overlay is supplied.

overlayServiceUrl.description: Optional: exact ESRI layer/service URL for the customer's own field to color-grade the map with, from a prior search_my_arcgis_maps/get_arcgis_map_layers result. Requires overlayFieldName to also be set. Only used to symbolize the map image — does not affect the fieldName ring-buffer averages above.

overlayFieldName.description: Optional: exact field name on overlayServiceUrl to color-grade by. Requires overlayServiceUrl.

overlayFieldType.description: Optional ESRI field type for overlayFieldName (e.g. "esriFieldTypeDouble"), from search_my_arcgis_maps results — helps pick appropriate class breaks.

overlayLegendTitle.description: Optional legend title for the overlay. Defaults to overlayFieldName if omitted.
